newsitem.title: USA: IBM stock climbs higher; unveils new product.
newsitem.headline: IBM stock climbs higher; unveils new product.

text.p: The stock of International Business Machines Corp. continued its upward trajectory on Tuesday as investors viewed the company as an increasingly safe technology investment.
In addition, Goldman Sachs initiated coverage of the computer giant by recommending the stock.
IBM was up $2.875 at $174.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange. More than 2 million shares had traded after 90 minutes of NYSE activity.
IBM hit a new all-time high in intra-day trading of $176.125, but then fell back slightly.

Goldman Sachs analyst Laura Conigliaro initiated coverage of IBM and added the stock to both Goldman's recommended list and its priority list, fuelling even more investor enthusiasm in the stock, traders said.
"It's all the positive momentum flowing into the stock," said one technology trader, who estimated that IBM's shares would probably close just under their all-time high.
Last week, after CEO Louis Gerstner held an upbeat meeting with Wall Street analysts, both Credit Suisse First Boston and Prudential Securities raised their price targets on IBM.
The stock hit an all-time high of $175.875 in August 1987, before the stock market crash of October 1987.
Conigliaro was not immediately available for further details on her coverage of IBM.
Also Tuesday, IBM unveiled its new ThinkPad 380 notebook computer series.
The "all-in-one" design integrates a hard drive, a floppy drive and a CD-ROM in one unit with a 12.1-inch screen and Pentium microprocessor.
The company said estimated retail prices for the ThinkPad 380 series would start at $2,199 depending on model and configuration.
On Sunday, IBM scored a major publicity coup after its Deep Blue supercomputer made chess history, defeating world chess champion Garry Kasparov in a highly publicised match.
